keyconfounds: All four source dtype/mode combinations are measured: Float32 keys from source uniform[0,1), full-range UInt32 keys, keys-only and keys+UInt32 original indices. Source defaultN=1048576 and100internal sorts preserved. MakefileN536870912 and other CLI sizes/options are unmeasured; custom group scan is currently fixed to1024 groups/defaultN, not a general sort-library replacement.

Native remains actual Thrust sort/sort_by_key API (compiled Thrust2.0.1, inspected arithmetic-key dispatch reaches CUB DeviceRadixSort). Native library kernel count, digit/pass policies and workspace sizes are not profiled. Do not infer an authored radix kernel from the benchmark label alone.

CUDA.jl reference replaces historical marker/PASS with a custom stable32-pass one-bit LSD algorithm: localzero rank scan, one-block block-offset scan, stable scatter;96launches/sort. All three Julia versions use this same algorithm, which differs from native vendor implementation. Native-vs-Julia speed differences cannot be attributed solely to abstraction.

Workspace policy differs: custom Julia temporary keys/local-prefix/group tables and optional values are preallocated outside ROI; native Thrust manages its own internal temporary storage inside the sort API. Both time a complete sorting operation plus device-wide completion, excluding input reset/transfers. Allocation-policy confound is explicit, not hidden as pure kernel-codegen effect.

Float32 source inputs are finite/nonnegative, so IEEE bit order equals numeric order. Custom raw-bit ranking is certified for this source domain, not arbitrary negative/NaN IEEE sorting. UInt32 keys retain all32bits onGPU; no Float32 integer emulation. Float64 artifacts serialize full UInt32 values exactly.

Originalkeybits option is advisory/printed but does not mask sort keys; default32 remains metadata. Keys-only scatter never loads/stores values; pairs carry actual originalUInt32index payloads. Source std::mt19937seed19937 distributions reproduced withC++ generators, identical inputs across models/modes.

Native original correctness checks only key sortedness. Study additionally checks complete sorted key array against independent CPU sort, all value indices form a full permutation and each sorted key equals its input key at returned index. Raw pair order is preserved, not canonicalized or replaced by checksums.

Thrust sort does not guarantee stable equal-key order (installed sort.h source documentation). Current native arithmetic/CUB output happens to match stable CPU indices for all captured trials:21369 Float32 and138 UInt32 duplicate adjacencies. All models match raw tie order on this fixture; no cross-version API stability guarantee claimed.

80 final artifacts checked:4cases×4models×5trials, with2097157Double values/keys-only case and4194309/pairs, including exact1048581/2097157-value input prefixes. Each artifact is the final result of a100-sort trial; intermediate99outputs are not individually serialized or independently audited, as source also validates final result only.

Each trial averages100 timed sorts, resetting source input withH2D copy outside each interval; one full-sort warmup precedes5inprocess trials and meanruns2–5. Four retained sample means, not400independent timing samples. No outlier removal or fastest selection; all raw outertrial averages retained.

Custom shared scratch is4096B per rank/scan kernel,1024threads/block;1024 rank/scatter blocks and one group-scan block. CUDA.jl/KA use static shared storage, JACC uses dynamic4096B and shared(template) copy/barrier. Scatter explicitly0B, separate LaunchSpecs avoid cached grid/resource mismatch. Actual registers/spills/occupancy/traffic unmeasured.

All device indices/shared/barriers are own framework APIs with pure Julia integer helpers; no foreign CUDA device intrinsics or operator library in Julia variants. CUDA host allocation/completion glue onlyNVIDIA tested. Native is vendor header-library interop, not identical implementation class.

JACC measured~9.1–9.4ms/sort vsCUDA.jl/KA~1.5–2.1ms; correctness is exact. Cause is unresolved without profiling; no invented allocation/shared-memory/occupancy diagnosis. Integer scan/bitwise sorting is not an ordinary floating-FLOP roofline workload.

One current reference/KA/JACC program candidate, four process/device-JIT checks each for fourdtype/mode cases; four authored generic kernel definitions but three active per case. Definitions, specializations, cases, sort passes/repeats and compiler repair iterations are distinct; compiler internal passes/specialization count unknown. No target feedback repairs.
